target_customer: Parents who want to give a child an Android phone with locked down calls, apps and location
problem: Parents wanted a cheap kid safe smartphone without $10 to $15 monthly parental control fees.
business_model: freemium consumer app with premium features planned

founders.name: Renat Gataullin
founders.background_notes: Worked on two startup projects in 2011 before Kytephone per a profile.

competitors.name: Carrier parental control and family locator services
competitors.what: carrier controls often powered by Location Labs, $10 to $15 per month

technical_complexity.rationale: A launcher style lockdown app plus web dashboard on Android; making the lock hard to escape was the main difficulty.

defensibility.rationale: Reviewers compared many similar tools and the app was Android only with a free tier; easy to copy.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Carriers already sold family controls; Android later gained built in restricted profiles and Google Family Link, not sourced here.

market_need_then: Parents paid $10 to $15 per month for carrier controls and reviewers noted the market for childproofing gadgets was getting crowded in mid 2012.

branding.domain_note: kytephone.com, product name Kytephone; YC lists company as BarSense, a separate legal or earlier name that no source explains

identity.visual_style: kid friendly app screens in press

brand_strength.rationale: Covered by TechCrunch, Adweek, Fox News and GeekDad at launch, but no lasting community or brand assets found.

outcome_analysis: Kytephone launched publicly in June 2012 as a free Android lockdown app after YC and a small seed. Launch coverage was broad but the product was Android only and easy to copy, and a secondary source says it shut down in August 2014. The cause is not public, so failure factors are left empty.
notes: Funding unverified: CB Insights lists one $20K YC seed in 2012-01; a TechCrunch based summary said just under $0.5M seed. Neither cross-checked, so no round recorded. Shutdown date of 2014-08-12 comes from one secondary review site. Site kytephone.com returned HTTP 522 when fetched. Cause of shutdown not public. YC page text describes the product as Kyte. Completeness pass: one seed round dated 2012-01 is recorded from a single database (CB Insights, which gives about $20K); amount left null because TechCrunch says just under $0.5M seed and the two conflict.
